newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just lower but looks to upside.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just lower but looks to upside.

text.p: The gold market seemed to have regained a little self- confidence on Wednesday morning after its recent scares, leading some dealers to look for higher prices.
The market had been shaken ever since the Australian central bank announced at the beginning of the month that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves over the previous six months.
One dealer said he forecast gold managing a $318.00-$322.00 per ounce range for the day, but added, "There are a lot of nervous people out there."
That was a significant change from earlier in the week when most dealers favoured a test of the $313.60 recently low.
Gold fixed at $319.50, just 75 cents off the Tuesday afternoon fix but about $1.00 above the New York close.
"The close was engineered lower in New York last night by one player who just offered and offered it down," a dealer said.

Although the yen's weakness against the dollar provoked bullion selling in Japan during the Asian trading day, short covering and some physical buying took the market fairly comfortably back above the New York level.
"The market is a bit confused. You wouldn't want to go too long with this guy selling in New York," a dealer said.
Also coming into the market was some hedge selling from Australian producers overnight, while hovering overhead was the threat of further central bank sales.
A firmer dollar was not helping gold's recovery and still-soaring stock markets offered much more attractive profit potential for investors than did bullion, dealers said.
"If gold can get through $322.50 then we could see $324 and then $330," one said, adding that the downside for Wednesday might be limited to $318.00.
Silver was ignored in morning business at a barely changed $4.31/$4.33 after a forecast fall on Tuesday failed to materialise.
"People probably got their fingers burned yesterday. Silver looks like a buy the dips market," a dealer said.
He added that a target would be $4.40, which silver had failed to breach several times in the past few weeks.
Platinum and palladium were firmer in markets that remained tight despite the resumption of Russian exports of the latter last week after a gap of over six months.
Platinum exports were expected to resume this week and the market was indicated at $405.50/$408.50, up about $2.50.
